text:
maria: FYI p99 jump hitting hosted API (us-east) since ~08:23 UTC, p99 ~2.4s, p95 ~980ms. Seeing request backlog on route /v1/generate :sadge:
liam: Observed queue depth bump on rt-pool-3, latency correlates with kernel switch log entries around same time.
sharma: I'm seeing a KV cache miss ratio spike for model-x: miss_rate jumped from 6% -> 28% between 08:22-08:26. Could be cache thrash.
maria: Ops-bot, did any rollout happen?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy finished on model-x v3.2 at 08:20 UTC (80% traffic). No rollbacks.
nina: Canary might have different kernel affinity; profiler shows more aux_kernel usage.
alex: Dumping kernel selector trace for a sample request: 
```
timestamp=1612345690 kernel=aux_kernel reason=seq_len>1024 fallback=main_kernel latency_ms=2100
timestamp=1612345691 kernel=aux_kernel reason=kv_cache_miss=true latency_ms=2300
```
liam: Key observation: aux_kernel has higher tail latency for mixed short/long sequences; continuous batching is pulling short requests into large batches causing serialization on aux path.
sharma: Also seeing redis (kvcache) connections hitting ephemeral max_fds on a few hosts, causing transient increased miss latency. Redis INFO: used_memory_rss: 1.9G, blocked_clients: 2.
maria: Can someone run a quick `redis-cli info` on pod rt-cache-7?
sharma: Ran it, output snippet: `connected_clients: 120, blocked_clients: 2, maxclients: 1024` nothing obvious but fd usage near kernel limit on that VM.
liam: I pushed a temporary routing override to prefer main_kernel for short sequences (<256) on canary hosts. Rolling in 2m.
nina: After override p95 dropped to 610ms on canary subset, p99 fell to 1.1s. Good sign.
ops-bot: autoscaler: ramped up rt-pool-3 by +2 pods at 08:40 UTC due to queue depth.
alex: Profiling heap and thread states on aux_kernel process; thread dump shows threads stuck in `kv_cache::wait_for_prefetch` with high syscall latencies (epoll_wait ~40-60ms).
sharma: Investigating host-level io wait and network card interrupts. One noisy tenant was running high embedding batch jobs on same rack (identified by tenant-id T-987).
maria: So root cause hypothesis: canary model variant changed kernel affinity -> more requests hit aux_kernel which is sensitive to KV cache misses and host IO -> noisy neighbor embedding jobs increased IO wait -> KV cache miss rate + dequeue -> increased p99.
liam: Next actions: 1) revert canary kernel affinity change for v3.2 2) alert infra to throttle/noisy tenant T-987 3) add short-sequence kernel routing rule temporarily 4) add KV cache fd and blocked_clients alert.
sharma: I've already requested tenant throttling via partner-ops; also opened a host-level ticket to investigate NIC interrupt handling on affected VMs.
nina: For longer term: we should add a kernel-selection canary test in CI that simulates KV cache pressure and embedding-heavy noisy neighbors.
maria: Agreed. Also add a quick dashboard: KV cache miss rate + aux_kernel p99 + blocked_clients per host.
alex: Logging snippet I grabbed for the worst request: `model=model-x request_id=abcd123 kernel=aux_kernel kv_miss=true batch_size=16 seq_len=64 latency_ms=2398` suggests batch_size+kv_miss combo is bad for aux path.
liam: Rolling rollback of the affinity change completed at 08:53 UTC. Metrics trending back: p95 ~540ms, p99 ~720ms as of 09:05 UTC.
maria: Thanks everyone. I'll create a follow-up doc with timeline, patches, and cost analysis of extra autoscale.
ops-bot: incident-tracker: created incident IN-2026-042 for Hosted API p99 spike, assignees: liam, sharma, nina.
liam: Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes, but marking as mitigated for now. :thumbsup:
